title: Emrys and the Bakery
premise: Jonah Sterling inherited her late father's vineyard along with his crushing debts, and she has learned to ration her heart like the last bottles of a bad vintage — carefully, and never all at once. When her family reunion looms, she hires Emrys, the warm, guarded baker from town, to pose as her partner for one weekend, expecting nothing but performance. But Emrys has secrets of her own: a shuttered bakery, a bankruptcy, and a belief that survival means never needing anyone. As harvest season ripens, fake affection turns inconveniently real, forcing both women to choose between the safety of self-containment and the terrifying cost of belonging — until the night of the vineyard's first harvest festival, where Jonah must bid on keeping the land with money she doesn't have while confessing a love she can't take back.
about_author: Theo Whitlock is the pen name of a former sommelier who traded tasting notes for love stories set among vines and flour-dusted counters. They write about people who are better at feeding others than feeding themselves.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She audits the vineyard's accounts and finds the harvest loan will come due before the first grapes sell. Her mother calls about the family reunion and its inevitable interrogation about her love life. Emotional beat: weary control masking quiet panic; Jonah resolves to fix everything alone, as always.

chapters.title: Flour on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Out of bread and out of patience, she walks into Emrys's bakery on the square and is disarmed by cinnamon, warmth, and a woman who remembers her order by the second visit. A small kindness — a free loaf 'for the road' — lodges under Jonah's skin. Beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Desperate after learning the reunion includes a partner-plus-one dinner, Jonah proposes a paid arrangement: Emrys poses as her girlfriend for one weekend. Emrys refuses twice, then names a price that stings — enough to restart her own dead dream. Beat: transactional pride hiding mutual curiosity.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Over wine in the dusty tasting room, they rehearse their story: how they met, first date, inside jokes. Emrys catalogs Jonah's tells — the way she deflects with logistics — and recognizes a fellow survivor. Beat: intimacy through invention; laughter that feels dangerously unscripted.

chapters.title: The Reunion Gate
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Arrival at her aunt's estate, hand in hand with a stranger who fits too well. Her brother Marcus probes; her grandmother watches like an appraiser. Emrys charms the table effortlessly, and Jonah feels something sourer than relief: jealousy of how easily Emrys belongs anywhere. Beat: exposure anxiety.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At dinner, asked how they knew, Emrys improvises a story so tender it silences the room — and herself. Later, on the porch, Jonah thanks her with a kiss that neither planned nor apologized for. Beat: the lie stops being containable; desire breaks protocol.

chapters.title: Sunday Morning Rules
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Driving home, they agree the kiss was 'for the audience' and draft rules: no real dates, no real feelings, contract ends at harvest festival. Both sign the fiction. That night Jonah rereads the rules like scripture. Beat: denial dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: What the Bakery Closed Over
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Flashback woven into present: the fire that took her bakery, the insurance that failed, the fiancée who left when the money did. Emrys came to this town to disappear into work. Now Jonah keeps showing up at closing time. Beat: grief surfacing; fear of wanting again.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The grapes begin to soften and color; so does the arrangement. Emrys starts bringing pastries to the vineyard 'on delivery routes' that don't exist. Workers tease them; Jonah doesn't correct anyone anymore. Beat: slow-burn warmth; the heart training itself despite orders.

chapters.title: The Appraiser's Visit
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The bank sends an evaluator; the vineyard may be worth less than the debt. Jonah hides the meeting from Emrys and works herself sick. When Emrys finds her asleep over spreadsheets, she stays the night — chastely, then not. Beat: crisis meets comfort; walls crack.

chapters.title: Pieces on Loan
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys realizes she's lending pieces of herself again — exactly what she swore off after losing everything once. She pulls back abruptly, cancels a promised visit, and reverts to brisk politeness at the counter. Beat: self-protection as sabotage; Jonah feels the withdrawal like weather.

chapters.title: Marcus Knows
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Marcus shows up at the vineyard having discovered the original ad Jonah posted hiring a fake date. He offers to cover her debt if she sells her share and comes home to the family business. Beat: blackmail wrapped in generosity; identity under siege.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Despite everything, Emrys brings her whole staff to help with the first pick when a storm threatens the crop. Working shoulder to shoulder with Jonah through the night, hands bleeding, laughing in the rain-soaked rows, she admits — silently — this is belonging. Beat: grace through labor.

chapters.title: The Argument in the Barrel Room
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Post-harvest adrenaline ignites: Jonah accuses Emrys of running; Emrys accuses Jonah of renting affection because she can't risk owning any. Old wounds laid bare — the debts, the fire, the fiancée, the father. Beat: climax of conflict; truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Contract's End
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys formally ends the arrangement, returning Jonah's payment untouched. 'You can't buy your way into being loved,' she says, and closes the bakery early for the first time ever. Jonah stands in the empty shop. Beat: rock bottom; the safe thing done painfully right.

chapters.title: The Offer She Should Take
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Marcus's deadline arrives: sign away the vineyard, erase the debt, return to the fold. Jonah nearly signs — the pen hovering — then looks at the first bottle of the vintage on her desk, labeled in Emrys's handwriting from a night she can't surrender. Beat: decision point; choosing risk over rescue.

chapters.title: First Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The festival opens the season; the whole town comes, including Emrys, working a pastry stall across the square. Jonah publicly toasts the vintage and, in front of everyone, tells the true story of how they met — no script, no payment. Beat: public vulnerability; reclaiming the narrative.

chapters.title: Bidding on Forever
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The charity auction for the harvest's first case becomes the stage: Jonah bids recklessly, wins, and gives the bottle to Emrys in front of the crowd, asking not for a date but for a beginning. Emrys, terrified and moved, doesn't answer — she kisses her. Beat: romantic climax.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival, Reckoned
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts her last fear: needing someone who could be taken. She opens her locked back room — the saved insurance settlement, her restart fund — and proposes they rebuild together: a bakery at the vineyard gate. Beat: trust as investment; two ledgers merged.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah declines Marcus's buyout with a counterplan: the festival sales, a new tasting-room partnership, and Emrys's capital keep the vineyard independent. Marcus, seeing his sister finally fight for something, softens and invests as family, not owner. Beat: resolution of external stakes.

chapters.title: What Rises in the Oven
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Construction begins on the bakery-vineyard storefront; mornings now start with shared coffee and unguarded talk. Emrys bakes the reunion dish that once fooled the family — now made honestly, for Sunday dinners that are real. Beat: domestic joy earned; identity rebuilt around belonging.

chapters.title: Vintage Year
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. One year later: the second harvest, the bakery thriving, the debt cleared. Jonah uncorks the auctioned first bottle and toasts the truth — that hearts aren't muscles to train but gardens to risk. They plant a new vine row named for the year everything changed. Beat: full-circle peace; love as harvest.
